sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), soluble in water; melting point of base 96 °C; racemic mixture.
White to pale yellowish crystalline powder.

Propranolol Hydrochloride: Developed by Sir James Black at ICI – the first successful beta-blocker, for which he shared the 1988 Nobel Prize in Medicine. First approval/introduction: Patented 1962; approved 1964 (ICI Pharmaceuticals). Etizolam: A thienotriazolodiazepine marketed in Japan, Italy and India; not approved in the USA or UK. First approval/introduction: Patented 1972; approved in Japan 1984 (Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical).
Propranolol 10 mg + Etizolam 0.25 mg; Propranolol 20 mg + Etizolam 0.5 mg

Propranolol controls peripheral (somatic) symptoms of anxiety such as tremor and tachycardia; etizolam relieves psychic anxiety and tension. The combination addresses both somatic and cognitive components.

Propranolol Hydrochloride Competitive antagonist at beta-1 and beta-2 adrenoceptors; reduces heart rate, myocardial contractility, renin release and sympathetic outflow; membrane-stabilising activity. Reduces somatic symptoms of anxiety and prevents migraine. Receptor / target profile: Non-selective competitive beta-1/beta-2 antagonist without intrinsic sympathomimetic activity; membrane-stabilising (sodium-channel) effect at high concentrations.

Etizolam Agonist at the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors, producing anxiolytic, hypnotic, muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant effects; potency ~6–10 times diazepam. Receptor / target profile: Positive allosteric modulator at the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors; clinically regarded as a benzodiazepine.
Extensive hepatic – CYP1A2, CYP2D6 (minor CYP2C19, CYP3A4); active 4-hydroxypropranolol
Summary: Well absorbed but extensive first-pass metabolism (bioavailability ~25%); Tmax 1–4 h (sustained-release longer). Lipophilic – crosses BBB. ~90% protein bound. Half-life 3–6 h (SR ~10 h).
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 0.5–2 h. Metabolised by CYP3A4 to active alpha-hydroxyetizolam. Half-life ~3.4 h (metabolite ~8 h).

Propranolol Hydrochloride: Bradycardia, hypotension, bronchospasm, hypoglycaemia, seizures, coma. Atropine, glucagon, supportive care. Etizolam: Somnolence, ataxia, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; flumazenil with caution.
Evidence derives from component data: propranolol for somatic anxiety (performance anxiety studies) and etizolam for generalised anxiety.
